brief: A Democratic sweep of both congressional chambers on Nov 4 stoked fears of a crackdown on AI spending and data-center buildouts. Rotation and hedge/vol unwinds let indices close higher that day despite an early slide. The Nov 5 cash open brought a second, sharper leg down. UBS says retail-led selling triggered systematic risk-control futures selling and leveraged-ETF unwinds, and Vanda confirms the largest 30-minute single-stock retail-selling episode since October. NDX broke below Election-night lows and its 200-day average. The SOX fell near 10% intraday. The AI basket is down 12% and NeoClouds 20% since the election. Hedge funds sold back hyperscaler positions bought the day before. UBS expects more retail selling and over $100 billion of Risk Control fund selling Friday, with the low possibly not in until Monday pre-open. Treasuries rallied on a fiscal thesis: political gridlock between a GOP White House and Democratic Congress implies less Treasury supply, reinforced by BofA pushing its coupon-auction-size-increase call from August to November. Oil rebounded on bets that Hormuz flows keep normalizing, though Brent flipped into contango. Analysts split. Wedbush Ives sees 10-12% more chip downside. Fundstrat Lee calls it an overreaction and sees a 20% tech rally.
